title: Latency regression playbook + alert + dashboard panels per model/route
creator: Priya Nadar
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a single operational surface that helps SRE/Platform and Product teams quickly triage and alert on latency regressions by model and route. Current dashboards show percentiles but lack a reproducible playbook and linked traces/metrics for root-cause. This ticket implements: (1) new dashboard panels that compare baseline vs current windows (p50/p95/p99) per model+route, with streaming vs non-streaming split; (2) a documented runbook for investigating regressions that links traces, kernel-level compute histograms, and queueing metrics; (3) alert rules for actionable regressions that reduce noise by correlating with deployment/route changes.

Goals:
- Fast root-cause for 80% of regressions (from 40% today) using one dashboard surface.
- Reduce false-positive latency alerts by 30% through correlated-signal checks.
- Provide clear handoff between on-call and eng owning model routes.

Success metrics (how we'll measure):
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for latency incidents on model routes decreases by 25% in first month after rollout.
- Precision of alerts (fraction that require remediation) increases by 30% in production tests.
- Dashboard adoption: at least 3 product/SRE teams use the panel in weekly reviews.

Technical approach / Implementation notes:
1) Data signals to pull together:
   - e2e request latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) computed over 1m/5m/1h windows per model+route.
   - io_mode tag (streaming | blocking) on all latency metrics so panels can split and compare.
   - kernel/compute latency histogram (per-inference compute time) from runtime telemetry.
   - queueing/backlog gauge (per-pool) and request batch size distribution.
   - linked traces (sampled distributed traces that include stage spans: ingress, routing, kernel, kv-cache, egress).
   - error count & type (timeouts, OOM, model-fallbacks) to help triage.

2) Metrics/log pipeline changes:
   - Add io_mode label at ingestion: instrument SDK edge and router to annotate streaming vs non-streaming at emit-time. (ENG-41791 partially started this.)
   - Ensure compute-time histograms are emitted with consistent buckets and tagged by model_version + instance_type.
   - Create an aggregated short-term store (rollup) for percentile diff comparisons (baseline window = previous 7 days same time-of-day).

3) Dashboard panels and interactions:
   - Top-level page: "Latency Regression Playbook (Model × Route)" with quick filters for model family, route, region, and deployment tag.
   - Panel A: grid of small-tiles (sparklines) per model+route showing p50/p95/p99 delta vs baseline; click tile opens detail.
   - Panel B: detail view for selected model+route showing stacked breakdown: client-perceived e2e latency, kernel compute, queue/wait, network proxy time; streaming vs blocking series overlay.
   - Panel C: fraction-of-requests-by-io_mode (to detect shifts in workload composition).
   - Panel D: linked trace list (N most recent traces that contributed to p95/p99) with one-click open in tracing UI.
   - Panel E: deployed-version and recent rollout timeline aligned with latency spikes.

4) Alerting playbook (how alerts are generated and suppressed):
   - Primary rule: p95 over 5m increased by >25% vs baseline AND absolute p95 > threshold for the route.
   - Noise suppression: require either (a) kernel compute median also increased by >20% OR (b) a change in route traffic composition (io_mode shift >15%) or recent deploy tag.
   - Auto-annotate alert with top correlated signals (compute histogram delta, backlog spikes, error spike) to speed triage.
   - Escalation: if p99 sustained > X for 15m, page on-call and create a ticket in the owning team's queue.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard deployed to console with all panels and crosslinks working.
- io_mode label is present on all new latency metrics for >=95% of traffic.
- Alert rules implemented and tested in staging with reduced noise compared to naive p95-only rule (show test summary).
- Runbook document exists and is linked from dashboard; includes step-by-step triage checklist.

Rollout plan:
1) Staging: wire metrics and temporary dashboard, run synthetic regressions to validate signal correctness (2w).
2) Canary: enable dashboard + alerts for two safety-critical routes (one streaming, one blocking) and run for 1 week. Collect alert precision/recall.
3) Gradual rollout by product-team adoption and feedback, full platform rollout after 3 weeks of canary.

Risks / Open questions:
- Instrumentation gaps for older SDKs: do we need a rollout policy to force label propagation? (Action: list client SDK owners).
- Baseline selection: 7-day vs 14-day; baseline may hide diurnal shifts for some workloads. Open: validate with users.
- Cost of storing high-cardinality histograms across many model versions. Might require sampling or cardinality limits.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/OBS-LatencyPlaybook (draft)
- Tracing UI mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/obs-trace-mockups
- GitHub proto PR (metrics): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/783
- Staging dashboard URL: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/latency-playbook/staging (internal)

Notes: prioritize accurate tagging and linked traces over fancy visuals. The immediate win is a reproducible triage path and lower alert noise.
comments: 2025-10-15 - Ethan Z: Initial spike completed; baseline aggregation pipeline prototype in telemetry PR (#783). Observed missing io_mode on ~8% of requests - tracking with SDK owners.
2025-10-20 - Priya N: Reviewed canary plan with SRE. Agreed to start with routes: /api/generate (blocking) and /api/stream-chat (streaming). Added due_date for canary completion.
2025-10-28 - QA: Ran synthetic regressions by slowing kernel by 30% for model-rlf-v1; dashboard detected p95 delta and linked traces correctly. Need better histogram bucket alignment.

2025-11-03 - Engineering review: Proposed alert thresholds adjusted downward after feedback; added 'require compute delta OR backlog spike' suppression rule to reduce noise. Assigning follow-up to ENG-44702 for histogram cost mitigation.
